outputs.L1: The present disclosure provides a display device comprising a display panel and a grating layer. The display panel includes a left display area and a right display area. From the center of a left-eye field-of-view central area toward a non-left-eye field-of-view central area within the left display area, the grating periods of the left-eye grating regions corresponding to a first color, a second color, and a third color each gradually decrease. Similarly, from the center of a right-eye field-of-view central area toward a non-right-eye field-of-view central area within the right display area, the grating periods of the right-eye grating regions corresponding to the first color, the second color, and the third color each gradually decrease.
outputs.L2: A display apparatus is disclosed that includes a display panel and a grating layer. The panel is divided into left and right display regions. Within the left display region, the grating pitches for first-, second-, and third-color left-eye grating regions progressively become smaller when moving from the center of the left-eye field-of-view central region toward an area outside that central region. Likewise, within the right display region, the grating pitches for first-, second-, and third-color right-eye grating regions progressively decrease from the center of the right-eye field-of-view central region toward an area beyond that central region.
outputs.L3:
The display device comprises a display panel and a grating layer. The display panel is divided into separate left and right display areas corresponding to the viewer’s left and right eyes, respectively.

Within the left display area, the grating layer includes three color-specific left-eye grating regions. The grating periods of these regions gradually decrease from the center of the central portion of the left-eye field of view toward its non-central portion.

Similarly, within the right display area, the grating layer includes three color-specific right-eye grating regions. The grating periods of these regions gradually decrease from the center of the central portion of the right-eye field of view toward its non-central portion.
outputs.L4:
A display device includes a display panel having a left-eye display area and a right-eye display area. A grating layer is disposed over the display panel and includes a first grating portion corresponding to the left-eye display area and a second grating portion corresponding to the right-eye display area. Each grating portion may be independently configured so that image light intended for one eye is directed toward that eye while image light intended for the other eye is controlled separately.

Each of the first and second grating portions includes multiple grating regions associated with different wavelength bands, such as red, green, and blue light. The grating period in each color-specific region varies according to position within the corresponding eye’s field of view. In particular, the grating period gradually decreases from a central field-of-view region toward one or more peripheral field-of-view regions. The rate or amount of variation may be selected independently for each color to account for wavelength-dependent diffraction behavior.

By providing separate, spatially varying gratings for the left and right display areas and for each color band, the device can more precisely control the propagation, diffraction, or extraction of image light across the display. The configuration may compensate for changes in viewing angle and optical response between central and peripheral regions, while also reducing color-dependent misalignment or nonuniformity. As a result, the display can provide improved image quality, color consistency, optical efficiency, and viewing performance throughout the field of view of each eye.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a display device having separate left-eye and right-eye display areas with color-specific grating periods that gradually decrease away from each eye’s field-of-view center.
counterfactuals.output: A display device includes a left-eye display area and a right-eye display area configured to provide image light to a left eye and a right eye, respectively. Each display area includes a plurality of gratings associated with respective color components of the image light. For each color component, the gratings have spatially varying grating periods that progressively decrease with increasing distance from a center of a field of view of the corresponding eye. The grating periods may be independently selected for different color components and for the left-eye and right-eye display areas to control propagation, diffraction, and output directions of the image light. The spatial variation in grating period may improve color alignment, pupil coverage, and image uniformity across the fields of view.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an optical display comprising a display panel and grating layer, where the grating periods for three colors vary spatially across left-eye and right-eye regions.
counterfactuals.output:
An optical display includes:

- a display panel having first, second, and third color subpixels; and  
- a grating layer disposed over the display panel and defining a left-eye region and a right-eye region.

The grating layer includes respective grating structures for light of the first, second, and third colors. Within each of the left-eye and right-eye regions, the grating period associated with each color varies as a function of position. The spatial variation is selected according to the wavelength of the corresponding color and the region’s intended viewing direction, such that light from the three color subpixels is directed toward the appropriate eye and substantially converges at a common viewing zone. The period profiles in the left-eye and right-eye regions may be different or mirror-symmetric to provide separate images to the viewer’s left and right eyes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise “present disclosure” summary of a stereoscopic display in formal patent language. Specify that the first-, second-, and third-color grating periods decrease from the central viewing area toward noncentral areas for both eyes.
counterfactuals.output: The present disclosure provides a stereoscopic display including first-, second-, and third-color gratings configured to direct respective color light toward left-eye and right-eye viewing areas. For each of the left-eye and right-eye viewing areas, grating periods of the first-, second-, and third-color gratings decrease from a central viewing area toward respective noncentral viewing areas.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into one patent-style paragraph: a display panel has left and right display areas, each with RGB grating regions whose periods become progressively smaller with distance from the corresponding eye’s field-of-view center.
counterfactuals.output: A display panel comprising a left-eye display area and a right-eye display area, each display area including a plurality of red, green, and blue grating regions arranged relative to a field-of-view center of a corresponding eye, wherein spatial periods of the red, green, and blue grating regions progressively decrease as a distance from the corresponding field-of-view center increases.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a dual-eye display device that uses a variable-period grating layer to provide separate left-eye and right-eye images, with all three color grating periods decreasing toward peripheral regions.
counterfactuals.output: A dual-eye display device includes a display panel configured to output left-eye and right-eye image light and a variable-period grating layer disposed in an optical path of the image light. The grating layer includes respective grating structures for first, second, and third color components, each having a spatially varying period configured to direct corresponding image light toward designated left-eye and right-eye viewing regions. The grating periods for all three color components decrease from a central region of the grating layer toward peripheral regions. The varying grating periods compensate for changes in propagation angle across the display aperture, thereby maintaining color alignment and separation of the left-eye and right-eye images over an expanded field of view.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
